source_text: Contra haec ergo verba mea, quae rescripseris audiamus: Non est ita ut loqueris, quicumque ista dixisti, non est ita; multum falleris, vel fallere meditaris; non liberum negamus arbitrium; sed: " vos Filius liberaverit - ait Veritas - tunc vere liberi eritis " [n178] . Hunc vos invidetis liberatorem, quibus captivis vanam tribuitis libertatem. " A quo enim quis devictus est - sicut dicit Scriptura - huic et servus addictus est " [n179] ; nec quisquam nisi per gratiam Liberatoris isto solvitur vinculo servitutis, a quo est hominum nullus immunis. "r unum quippe hominem peccatum intravit in mundum, et per peccatum mors; et ita in omnes homines pertransiit, in quo omnes peccaverunt " [n180] . Amplissimam esse nostri negotii dignitatem, ut ipsa rerum consideratio et appensio indicat, quas tuemur, ita etiam vester pavor; qui contra nostrorum sanguinem, pecuniarum effusione, haereditatum largitate, equorum transmissione, populorum seditione, potestatum corruptione pugnantes, et fidem vestram quae a nobis impugnatur, erubescitis profiteri, et ad nostrae sententiae, a qua deviastis, verba confugitis.
pass_a_gloss: Against these words of mine therefore, let us hear what you have written back: It is not so as you speak, whoever you are who said these things, it is not so; you are much deceived, or you meditate to deceive; we do not deny free choice; but: If the Son shall have freed you — Truth says — then you will be truly free. This liberator you begrudge, to whom as captives you attribute a vain liberty. For by whom anyone has been conquered — as Scripture says — to this he has also been bound a slave; nor is anyone loosed from this bond of slavery except through the grace of the Liberator, from which none of humans is immune. Through one human indeed sin entered into the world, and through sin death; and so it passed through unto all humans, in whom all sinned. That the dignity of our business is most ample, as the very consideration and weighing of the things which we guard indicates, so also your fear; you who fighting against the blood of ours by pouring-out of moneys, largesse of inheritances, sending-across of horses, sedition of peoples, corruption of powers, both blush to profess your faith which is attacked by us, and flee to the words of our sentence, from which you have deviated.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS arbitrium=judgment, free decision; Blaise liberum arbitrium
LS liber=free; Blaise unde liberum est abstinere
LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'

pass_b_english: Let us hear, then, what you wrote in reply to these words of mine: “It is not as you say, whoever said this; it is not so. You are greatly mistaken, or planning to mislead. We do not deny free choice. But Truth says: ‘If the Son sets you free, then you will be truly free’ (John 8:36). You begrudge this liberator to the captives to whom you attribute an empty freedom. ‘For whatever has overcome someone has made him its slave’, as Scripture says (2 Peter 2:19). No one is released from this bond of slavery except through the liberator's grace, and no human being is exempt from it. ‘For through one man sin entered the world, and through sin death; and so it passed to all human beings, in whom all sinned’” (Romans 5:12; Augustine, On Marriage and Concupiscence 2.8).

The cause we defend has the greatest dignity, as consideration and weighing of the matters themselves show, and as your fear also shows. You fight to shed our people's blood by pouring out money, giving away estates, sending horses, stirring up the populace, and corrupting officials. Yet you are ashamed to profess the faith of yours that we attack, and take refuge in the language of our position, from which you have strayed.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Glossary default: arbitrium is the decision-power, not a later Augustinian/Reformation free-will locus.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied.
